title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 153 (Application for allotment of Director Identification Number)

content.overview: Section 153 requires every individual intending to be appointed as a director of a company to make an application for allotment of a Director Identification Number (DIN) in the prescribed form and manner to the Central Government, with the prescribed fee.
content.glance: Every individual intending to be a director must apply for a DIN in the prescribed form with fee; one person, one DIN.
content.study: Every individual intending to be appointed as a director of a company shall make an application for allotment of Director Identification Number to the Central Government in such form and manner and along with such fees as may be prescribed. A person holds only one DIN. Appointment under section 152 cannot proceed without a DIN allotted under section 154. Current-law framing: identify the individual intending appointment; confirm application in prescribed form with fee; link to allotment under s. 154 and appointment under s. 152.

sections.heading: Who Must Apply
sections.body: Every individual intending to be appointed as a director of a company.

sections.heading: Application
sections.body: Application to the Central Government in the prescribed form and manner with prescribed fee.

sections.heading: One DIN
sections.body: A person is allotted and holds only one Director Identification Number.

sections.heading: Link to Appointment
sections.body: Without a DIN, appointment under section 152 cannot be completed; consent and DIN are filed with the appointment.

provisions.title: Application for allotment of Director Identification Number

examples.title: First-time applicant
examples.body: A person intending to become a director for the first time applies for a DIN in the prescribed form with fee under s. 153.

examples.title: No DIN, no appointment
examples.body: A company attempts to appoint a director who has not applied for or been allotted a DIN. Section 152 read with s. 153 blocks the appointment.

hypotheticals.question: Can the same individual hold two DINs for two different companies?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. A person is allotted and holds only one DIN, which is used across companies.

distinctions.title: Application for DIN (s. 153) vs allotment of DIN (s. 154)
distinctions.right: Central Government’s duty to allot within prescribed time

misconceptions.trap: DIN is optional if the person is already a director of another company under the old regime without one.
misconceptions.correction: Every individual intending to be appointed as a director must have a DIN; appointment without DIN is not permitted under the s. 152/153 scheme.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 153 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the individual intending appointment. II. Confirm application in prescribed form with fee. III. Link to allotment (s. 154) and appointment (s. 152). IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Application facts; form/fee compliance; DIN status; precise relief.
